name: WebGPU (in-browser inference)
notable_features: WebGPU is a web standard for GPU compute and graphics, enabling in-browser LLM inference
Compute shaders enable GEMM operations needed for transformer inference
WGSL (WebGPU Shading Language) is the compute shader language
WebLLM and transformers.js are the primary LLM frameworks using WebGPU
No installation required - runs in the browser with GPU access
hardware_caveats: Performance is 2-5x slower than native GPU inference due to browser overhead
Memory is limited by browser tab memory constraints (typically 2-4GB)
No access to system RAM - all model weights must fit in GPU memory or be streamed
Browser support is recent - Safari 18+ (2024), Firefox 141+ (2025)
No continuous batching or paged KV cache - single-stream inference only
WGSL is less mature than CUDA/Metal - fewer optimized kernels
best_for: Zero-install LLM inference in the browser
Web applications that need local inference without server dependency
Cross-platform deployment (Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS) via browser
Small models (1-7B) that fit in browser memory constraints
avoid_for: Large models (70B+) - browser memory constraints are too tight
Maximum performance - native GPU inference is 2-5x faster
Production serving - no batching, scheduling, or multi-tenant support
notes: WebGPU enables in-browser LLM inference via compute shaders. The primary frameworks are WebLLM (MLC) and transformers.js (Hugging Face). Performance is 2-5x slower than native GPU inference due to browser overhead and WGSL immaturity. Memory is limited by browser tab constraints (typically 2-4GB). WebGPU is the right choice for zero-install web applications and small models, but not for large-scale or high-performance local inference.
